subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu streaming card full-content updates cause severe latency regression on long replies

question: Should Feishu streaming cards remain full-content-only with another performance mitigation, or should OpenClaw add an explicit append/delta opt-in for deployments where full-content CardKit updates are too slow?
rationale: The official CardKit contract and prior truncation fix favor full-content updates, but the latest live repro says cadence coalescing did not solve the severe latency, and adding a new config mode is compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Require a Feishu contract decision first
options.body: Keep the issue open, pause new automated fixes, and ask Feishu owners to review redacted live logs before choosing full-content backpressure or append-mode support.

options.title: Continue full-content mitigation only
options.body: Reject append mode for now and require a revised full-content fix with proof that long replies improve without content truncation.

options.title: Accept an append-mode opt-in
options.body: Allow a documented non-default append/delta mode with focused tests and live proof, while preserving full-content as the default for tenants that need it.

recommendation.title: Require a Feishu contract decision first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open, pause new automated fixes, and ask Feishu owners to review redacted live logs before choosing full-content backpressure or append-mode support.

likelyOwner.reason: The package metadata names this handle as the Feishu plugin maintainer, and the decision is specific to Feishu channel behavior and compatibility.
